reason: The source names release-tagged work but does not define per-step prerequisite CheckViews or a failure-to-scope decision table. More critically, current public owners do not expose a truthful, composable inference/native/capture prerequisite receipt at the CLI boundary. A new selector accepting caller-supplied CheckViews or readiness flags would merely restate fixture inputs; a new cross-owner evidence transport is a protocol-sized scope beyond the bounded two-hour unit.

sourceStepLabels.stepTagInterpretation: §1.1 defines deliverables/prerequisites by release: R0 evidence and gates; R1 minimum journal/archive; R2 complete store; R3 full client integration; R4 recorder; R5 optional pilots/repair-generated changes. §20 tags build rows as above. AT-lifestore-70 itself is included in step 1 exit, so it cannot be treated as its own precondition. The spec does not define a persisted current-release value or what outcome a selector returns when an individual prerequisite fails.

currentReleaseSemantics.existingType: @toy/contracts Release is only the enum R0-R5; it is not a selected/current release record.
currentReleaseSemantics.existingInputs: CLI research.check, status/doctor and stack.up can accept a requested release target; this is a caller-selected query/setup target, not current installed or admitted release state.
currentReleaseSemantics.selectorImplication: If later specified, select from a source-bound step identifier and derive its bracketed release tag from the Life Store build plan. Do not accept a caller release tag, readiness flags, or supplied CheckViews as authority. No such current command/API exists today.

interfaceAndCases.currentContract: No LifeStoreBuildStepId or LifeStoreBuildSelection DTO. Existing Release R0-R5 is too broad to identify a step. No existing public owner accepts/returns a source-bound step selection.
interfaceAndCases.currentCli: No build.select/build-selection command in cli-declarations.ts or cli/src/main.ts. Existing release.status and release.rollback do not select build work.
interfaceAndCases.candidateSyntaxOnlyIfTheSpecIsAmended: toy build select lifestore --step <source-step-id> --json; step ID maps to exactly one source row and its tag is derived from the pinned source. This is not an implementation instruction or currently valid Toy CLI syntax.
interfaceAndCases.minimumMissingContract: Before source admission, the spec must define canonical step IDs, source digest binding, exact prerequisite owner CheckView IDs and evidence freshness rules for each step, and deterministic proceed/blocked/deferred results when any required check is failed, missing, or NOT_IMPLEMENTED. A real owner transport must supply those checks; callers cannot submit the checks or outcome flags.
interfaceAndCases.finiteCasesDerivableToday: Only the source tag matrix above is derivable. The source lists acceptance exits per row but does not specify their conversion into prerequisite CheckViews or a finite failure-to-scope matrix. The literal AT-70 Given/When/Then therefore cannot be given truthful positive CLI cases using current owners.
requiredBehaviorOnceSpecified: For each source step row, prove selection is bound to the exact current Life Store spec digest and yields only that row's R0/R1/R2/R5 scope.
For a failed inference prerequisite, prove only the spec-defined allowed scope proceeds and all unsupported inference-dependent work is blocked.
For failed resource admission, prove the spec-defined scope is blocked while preserving permitted lower-resource work.
For absent/failed native prerequisite, prove native-dependent scope is deferred without changing the source step tag.
For failed or absent R1 capture/incident owner, prove R1 capture is retained or the selection blocks exactly as a clarified spec directs; current text does not settle this result.
Assert R2 full-store activation, R3 app integration, R4 recorder integration, and R5 optional pilot/auto-promotion remain independently gated at their source tags.

sourceAdmissionBoundary.why: Do not create a DTO, release selector, generic aggregator, or fixture-only inspection probe until the missing source contract and real owner transports are specified. A selector-only patch would satisfy the ordinal-to-tag mapping but not the failed-prerequisite behavior in AT-lifestore-70.
